name: bird-transport
title: BiRD reactor transport refactor for cell-engine coupling
description:
The current BiRDReactorProcess owns biomass internally via a Monod ODE,
which conflicts with a cell engine that also owns biomass; today this is
worked around with a bird_disable_internal_biomass flag. This
investigation replaces that with a single-responsibility split: a shared
transport module, the existing BiRDReactorProcess kept for standalone use
(transport + an extracted MonodCellProcess), and a new BiRDTransportProcess
that takes biomass/substrate/dissolved gas as inputs and emits only the
transport contribution.

The four phases proceed from the refactor (Phase 1, which also yields the
MonodCellProcess that serves as the trivial cell-side fixture per the
cell-side interface contract), to an integration test that the closed
loop fires at impactful biomass (Phase 2), to making the coupling interval
tunable (Phase 3), to supporting the stirred-tank geometry of the target
benchmark (Phase 4). This is the upstream reactor-physics dependency for
the v2ecoli multiscale-bioprocess study mbp-03, which declares
pbg-bioreactor-transport-fork as a hard prerequisite.
question:
Can the BiRD 0D reactor physics be refactored so that biomass is an
input — an external cell engine owns growth and substrate exchange while
the reactor process owns only gas–liquid transport — and does the
resulting coupled system exercise the reactor→cell feedback that a
single-process reactor cannot?
hypothesis:
Extracting the shared transport physics (kLa, Higbie, Henry, Wilke–Chang)
into a module consumed by BiRDReactorProcess (transport + internal Monod,
standalone) and a new BiRDTransportProcess (transport only,
biomass-as-input) preserves the standalone reactor's behavior exactly and
enables a coupled configuration in which dissolved O2 responds to
externally supplied biomass. At a density where consumption exceeds
transport supply, dissolved O2 drops below saturation and O2 mass balance
closes across the cell and reactor contributions.

studies.name: bird-01-transport-process
studies.title: Transport-process split
studies.question:
Can the gas–liquid transport physics be extracted into a shared module
and exposed as a biomass-as-input BiRDTransportProcess that emits only
the transport contribution, while the standalone BiRDReactorProcess (now
transport + an extracted MonodCellProcess) keeps its pre-refactor
behavior?
studies.claim: The gas-liquid transport physics is cleanly extracted: the standalone BiRDReactorProcess reproduces the pre-refactor trajectories, while the transport-only BiRDTransportProcess emits zero biomass delta, kLa-driven O2 transport, zero glucose transport, and symmetric CO2 stripping - biomass ownership sits entirely with the cell engine.

biological_validation.basis: All 6 per-edge behavior verifiers pass (tests/test_bird01_transport.py): zero biomass delta, O2 transport == kLa*(C*-C), zero glucose, symmetric CO2, standalone regression preserved, and the MonodCell contract.

regression_compatibility.basis: Workspace builds and the full suite is green (51 passed); the baseline composite runs cleanly through the workbench.

explanatory_gain.basis: Confirms the single-responsibility split composes at shared stores under PBG update aggregation without either process owning the other's state.

studies.name: bird-02-closed-loop-liveness
studies.title: Closed-loop liveness
studies.question:
When BiRDTransportProcess is coupled to the Phase-1 MonodCellProcess at a
static high biomass density, does the reactor→cell feedback fire —
dissolved O2 dropping below saturation as consumption outpaces transport —
with O2 mass balance closing across cell and reactor contributions?
studies.claim: Coupling the transport process to the Monod cell at high biomass fires the reactor->cell feedback - dissolved O2 drops below air saturation as consumption outpaces transport - and recovers toward saturation when biomass is removed; the O2 mass balance closes.

biological_validation.basis: Behavior verifiers pass (tests/test_bird02_liveness.py): DO drops below saturation at high biomass, O2 mass balance residual ~0, and DO recovers to the saturation band when biomass is removed.

regression_compatibility.basis: Workspace builds and the full suite is green (51 passed); the baseline composite runs cleanly through the workbench.

explanatory_gain.basis: Demonstrates a live closed loop: the reactor and cell engine exchange dissolved O2 additively at the shared store, so net dO2/dt = transport - consumption is exercised at impactful density.

studies.name: bird-03-coupling-interval
studies.title: Coupling-interval convergence
studies.question:
Can the reactor coupling/update interval be exposed as a tunable parameter,
and does the coupled trajectory converge as the interval decreases?
studies.claim: The reactor coupling/update interval is a tunable parameter, and the coupled trajectory converges as the interval decreases (dt -> 0).

biological_validation.basis: Behavior verifiers pass (tests/test_bird03_coupling_interval.py): the coupling interval is configurable, and the trajectory converges as the interval is refined.

regression_compatibility.basis: Workspace builds and the full suite is green (51 passed); the baseline composite runs cleanly through the workbench.

explanatory_gain.basis: Establishes numerical trust in the coupled scheme: results are interval-independent in the fine-dt limit, so the coupling interval is a convergence knob rather than a hidden model parameter.

studies.name: bird-04-reactor-geometry
studies.title: Reactor geometry & axial structure
studies.question:
Can the reactor support a stirred-tank kLa correlation (the benchmark
geometry) alongside the bubble-column form, selectable by configuration?
studies.claim: The reactor supports a stirred-tank (Van't Riet) kLa correlation alongside the bubble-column (Higbie) form, selectable by configuration; a depth-resolved 1D column additionally resolves the axial O2/biomass structure the 0D model cannot express.

biological_validation.basis: Behavior verifiers pass (tests/test_bird04_geometry.py): geometry is selectable via config and kLa matches the stirred-tank correlation. The new BiRDColumn1DProcess (tests/test_column1d.py) adds a real axial gradient (sparger-high, monotone, geometry-dependent).

regression_compatibility.basis: Workspace builds and the full suite is green (51 passed); the baseline composite runs cleanly through the workbench.

explanatory_gain.basis: Shows one process family spans well-mixed geometries AND a 1D depth-resolved column, so the same transport correlations drive both lumped and spatially-resolved reactor designs.
